title: He Can't Code but His AI Agents Make Him $5K/Month
channel: Chris Koerner on The Koerner Office Podcast
promo_conflict: Vadim is promoting his own beta product, Vugola. Its results and market claims are self-reported and unverified.

stated_problem.quote: The clipping process takes too long.
stated_problem.speaker: Vadim

idea.name: Vugola
idea.one_liner: Subscription software for clippers, marketers, podcasters and streamers to create, schedule and caption short clips, with a planned agentic clipping workflow.
idea.customer: Clippers, marketers, podcasters, streamers and other creators who want to distribute short-form video.
idea.offer: An all-in-one clipping, scheduling and captioning tool; Vadim also describes a future workflow in which agents find source videos, create clips and schedule posts.
idea.revenue_model: Monthly subscriptions at three tiers, with quarterly or yearly upsells and one-time credit purchases.

key_quotes.quote: Hey, I'm Vadim and I'm the founder of Vugola, which is a clipping starter for clippers and marketers
So it's a clipping scheduling captioning to allin-one.
And now we have a couple hundred paying users now.
The clipping process takes too long.
the future of clipping is not going to be like human clippers. It's literally going to be agent clippers clipping for you.

claims.claim: Vadim reported $5,000 in revenue in the previous 30 days.
claims.quote: Yeah, so in the last 30 days I made $5,000.

claims.claim: Vadim said the software had generated more than 10,000 clips.
claims.quote: We've generated I think over like 10,000 plus clips and like so far the growth has been pretty steady.

claims.claim: Vadim acquired 450 free users and received feedback from them.
claims.quote: that's how I got my first 450 like free users on my software and got a bunch

claims.claim: Vadim reported 267 paying users.
claims.quote: And right now we have like 267 paying users right now.

claims.claim: The three subscription tiers were $9, $39 and $99 per month.
claims.quote: So, first is like a $9 plan and then it's a $39 plan and it's a $99 plan. So, for each monthly Yeah.

claims.claim: Vadim said an upsell change led to a day with about $900 in revenue.
claims.quote: I think like one day I made like a like like 900 bucks just like in one day after I made like the upselling perks and features

claims.claim: Vadim estimated that users may cancel after one to three months.
claims.quote: if you liked it or not they're going to leave probably within the like the first two to three months probably

claims.claim: Vadim reported profit margins as 80% to 85%, though the transcript phrasing is unclear.
claims.quote: And how much of that was profit? 85 80% profit margins.

claims.claim: Vadim described 70% to 80% as an ideal SaaS margin target.
claims.quote: making sure hey like if I package it in this amount of price this amount of credits like ideally you want 70 to 80% profit margins in the SAS world.

claims.claim: Vadim said he spent $500 worth of monthly credits in four days while building.
claims.quote: Like I said like I spent like $500 of the monthly credits in the span of 4 days.

claims.claim: Vadim said his Claude Code Max subscription cost $200 per month.
claims.quote: Yeah, I'm using cloud code max subscription. So I'm paying 200 bucks a month.

claims.claim: Vadim said the coding plan cost $250 on mobile and $200 on the web app.
claims.quote: So when I first got cloud uh cloud code, if you buy it on the mobile app, it's 250 bucks. I don't know why, but then if you buy it in the web app, it's 200 bucks.

claims.claim: Vadim said a Codex plan was another $200.
claims.quote: and then I go to Codeex and another Codeex $200 plan

claims.claim: Vadim claimed a $200 plan provided about $15,000 worth of credits and tokens.
claims.quote: when you buy the $200 a month plan, they're giving you like $15,000 worth of actual credits and tokens.

claims.claim: Vadim estimated the agents doing work for Vugola cost $200 to $400 per month.
claims.quote: And I have agents doing this for me all for like 200 bucks a month 400 bucks a month like everything for my own behalf.

claims.claim: Vadim estimated that replacing an agent-run department with a human job would cost $50,000 to $70,000 per year.
claims.quote: this is easily like a 50 60k 70k a year job just for like one department of bugola like moderating fulltime.

claims.claim: Vadim said his Twitter personal brand had about 27,000 followers.
claims.quote: I built up my personal brand on Twitter to like 27,000 followers and then I started posting on Instagram.

acquisition_channels.details: Vadim said he marketed organically on X/Twitter; he also started posting short-form videos on Instagram, YouTube Shorts and TikTok.
An agent found Reddit, LinkedIn and X users discussing clipping tools, then Vadim sent them DMs offering a free trial.

ideas.delivery: Vugola processes uploaded or linked long-form video into short clips, captions and scheduled posts. Vadim describes using Gemini API for video and transcript analysis, and says agents could eventually handle clipping and scheduling tasks.

uk_legal_risk.reason: The described acquisition included unsolicited DMs to people discussing clipping tools. If recipients are UK individuals or sole traders, social DMs used for direct marketing are prohibited under PECR.

ideas.other_uk_rules: UK GDPR applies to account, video and analytics data. UK subscription cancellation and renewal requirements under the DMCC Act may apply.

idea.name: Performance-paid clipping service

idea.customer: Streamers, podcasters and other creators seeking reach through short-form video.
idea.offer: Repurpose long-form content into clips and distribute them through multiple accounts; clippers are paid per thousand views.
idea.revenue_model: Performance-based CPM payments from clients or campaigns fund payments to clippers; exact service margin is not stated.

key_quotes.quote: If the Clippers get paid a dollar per thousand views and then the client gets like 100 million views, it's a win-win.
if you have Clippers, they make up like 50 sub accounts in your name, repurpose all the like they clip like they bunch of clips to show content on all 50

claims.quote: If the Clippers get paid a dollar per thousand views and then the client gets like 100 million views, it's a win-win.

idea.name: Content Rewards
idea.one_liner: A platform for clipping campaigns that tracks posted clip views and pays clippers on a CPM basis.
idea.customer: Creators or campaign owners seeking clips, and clippers who want performance-based payouts.
idea.offer: Clippers submit social post links to campaigns; the platform tracks views and pays according to CPM.
idea.revenue_model: Not stated for the platform; clippers are described as receiving view-based payouts.

key_quotes.quote: You take that like Instagram link, Tik Tok post link and then you just submit it on content rewards.
And that's how they start tracking you for your views and giving you like a CPM which they pay you like 10 cents, 30 cents or whatever, like a dollar per thousand views.

claims.claim: The speaker said clippers could be paid 10 cents, 30 cents or about $1 per thousand views.
claims.quote: And that's how they start tracking you for your views and giving you like a CPM which they pay you like 10 cents, 30 cents or whatever, like a dollar per thousand views.

idea.name: Automated lead generation with agents
idea.one_liner: An agentic workflow that finds leads daily, messages them and follows up for a business.
idea.customer: Businesses or sales teams seeking leads; the transcript does not specify a niche.
idea.offer: An agent running on a daily cron job to find, message and follow up with leads.

key_quotes.quote: I can build a agent that literally goes and has like a cron job.
So itely runs every single day and it can go find me leads on my own behalf.
It can go message those leads and go follow up with those leads.

ideas.delivery: An AI agent runs on a daily schedule, finds leads, messages them and follows up.

uk_legal_risk.reason: The workflow explicitly messages and follows up with leads, but the channel and recipients are unspecified. Cold SMS, WhatsApp or social DMs to UK individuals or sole traders are prohibited under PECR; the transcript does not establish a compliant channel.

ideas.other_uk_rules: UK GDPR applies to personal data used to identify and contact leads. Cold email is allowed only to limited companies with an opt-out; cold calls must screen TPS/CTPS.
